mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDPC1 (demand) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as rising corporate demand signals stronger economic growth and investor confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained GDPC1 growth, or during recessions when demand growth is present but returns remain flat.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained crossing of FEDFUNDS above 4.5% triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher interest rates compress equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.5%, or the effect persists for less than 20 days post-trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly rises in FEDFUNDS (easing) and CPIAUCSL (inflation) predict negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as conflicting signals reduce market confidence.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite both proxies rising, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained drop in UNRATE below 3.0% predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as lower unemployment benefits reduce labor market pressures.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.0% in late-cycle expansion regime
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when UNRATE drops below 3.0% in such regimes, or the effect reverses in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (supply) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as rising production signals robust economic activity and corporate profitability.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during sustained INDPRO growth, or during contraction periods when supply growth is present but returns remain flat.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained crossing of PAYEMS above 150,000 predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as higher employment signals labor market strength and consumer spending potential.
failure_condition: 5-day returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite PAYEMS exceeding 150,000, or the effect fades within the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly rises in GDPC1 (demand) and HOUST (industrial production) predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as combined demand and production growth signals robust economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite both proxies rising, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-stage tightening cycle, a sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.5% predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as reduced rate pressure eases financial constraints.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5% in late-stage tightening cycle
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS drops below 1.5% in such regimes, or the effect reverses in subsequent months.
